label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

In handleClick, exportReport(...).then(...) only resets `busy` on success; there's no .catch or .finally, so when the fetch rejects (non-2xx status throws), setBusy(false) is never called and the button stays disabled until the page is reloaded. The fix is to reset `busy` in a finally block and surface an error toast on failure.

input.title: Re-enable the export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

In `handleClick`, `exportReport(reportId, format).then(...)` only has a success handler, so `setBusy(false)` never runs when the promise rejects (e.g. a non-2xx response from the server, which `exportReport` turns into a thrown error). The button is left disabled (greyed out) until the page is reloaded.

Add a failure path that also clears the busy state, for example by adding a `.catch()` (or `.finally()` for the `setBusy(false)` call) alongside the existing `.then()`, and ideally surface the error to the user via the existing toast helper (e.g. `toast.show(t("ui.export.failed"), "error")`) so a failed export is both recoverable and visible.
